solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Screen vegetable on the turn for one?

definitions.text: Screen vegetable on the turn for one?

indicators.note: something on the turn is changing or going bad, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: all fifteen letters of the two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip: use a screen to keep out flies from vegetables that are starting to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the two first words rearrange, and the clue as a whole describes an insect that would feed on a vegetable that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger beetle feeds on decaying matter, so a rotting vegetable is just the kind of thing it would be found eating.

clue.text: Sadistic sort disgusted by love

parts.note: sick, as in 'sick of it', means disgusted
love is zero in tennis, a letter O

explanation.surface: A cruel person who is repelled by affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicko is informal for a perverted or cruel person, so a sadistic type fits the slang term.

clue.text: One absorbing shock of a source hiding IRA brief

indicators.note: hiding means keeping something inside, so one piece goes within the other
something brief is cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the initials with the final letter cut
a spring is a source of water

explanation.surface: Something that takes the shock out of a news source keeping quiet about the IRA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A spring' together forms the outer piece, with the shortened initials slipped between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An air spring is a suspension device using compressed air, so it is a component that absorbs jolts in a vehicle.

clue.text: Woman who earned money from her bed?

definitions.text: Woman who earned money from her bed?

parts.words: Woman who earned money from her bed?
parts.note: surface reading: a woman paid for what goes on in her bedroom, hinting at the oldest profession
setter's reading: a British artist whose unmade bed, exhibited in 1999, was later sold for millions

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests something seedy, but Tracey Emin's installation 'My Bed', shortlisted for the Turner Prize, sold at auction for over two million pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracey Emin is the artist whose famous installation of her own rumpled bed brought her a fortune.

clue.text: Vessel girl at work filled with headless beer

indicators.note: filled with says another piece is placed inside these
without its head, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
ale with its first letter removed
a machine at work is on

explanation.surface: A girl at her job on a ship, full of beer that has lost its froth.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl and at work join as an outer pair, with the beheaded ale filling the gap between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship of the 15th to 17th centuries, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Succeed in ignoring bit of blubbing and end the conversation

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to bring off something is to succeed in doing it

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter, here its opening one

parts.note: first letter of blubbing

explanation.surface: Pulling it together on a tearful phone call and hanging up.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the B from the phrase for succeed to leave the British expression for hanging up the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring off is British idiom for putting down the phone, which ends a telephone call.

clue.text: Teacher receiving nothing after spreadsheet that's excellent

parts.note: Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet program

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the next piece goes inside

parts.note: sir is the name pupils use for a male teacher
nothing is zero, letter O

explanation.surface: A teacher scores zero after producing a spreadsheet, and that is a fine result.
explanation.definitionFit: Excelsior can mean of the highest quality, so it serves as a superlative of praise.

clue.text: African expresses disapproval with Indian leader

parts.note: tuts is the sound and verb for clicking the tongue in disapproval

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Indian

explanation.surface: Someone from Africa frowns on an Indian politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi, so a member is an African.

clue.text: Enduringly popular cut first released by Young?

indicators.note: releasing the first means letting go of the opening letter

parts.note: sever, meaning cut, without its first letter
green means young and inexperienced

explanation.surface: A timeless track, first put out by a singer called Young.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Young suggests Neil or Will Young, but it is just an adjective; cut in the surface reads as a recorded track.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen song or show stays popular year after year, like a tree that keeps its leaves.

clue.text: My face is warm and friendly

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
dial is slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: Someone describing their own pleasant expression.
explanation.walkthrough: My looks like a possessive but is an exclamation; cor is an informal British cry of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial describes behaviour that is genial and sincere, a synonym of the definition phrase.

clue.text: Fashion accessory Bond put on cheek

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or nerve
a tie is a bond or link

explanation.surface: James Bond dressing up a cheeky look with something stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond, with its capital, suggests 007; it simply means a tie. In an across answer, put on means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is worn around the collar as part of a smart outfit, an item of dress beyond the basics.

clue.text: It is my fault old soprano hampers work

indicators.note: to hamper is to hem something in, so these letters enclose another piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
standard abbreviation for old
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: An apology: an elderly singer is getting in the way of the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation someone makes on realising they have made a blunder themselves.

clue.text: Reforming band to cover Cast, Mud and ELO

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so the band surrounds the rest

parts.note: a ring is a circular band

indicators.note: to cast metal is to remould it into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band getting back together to play covers of Cast, Mud and Electric Light Orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast, Mud and ELO are all British pop groups, so 'Cast' looks like a third band in the list; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To remould is to shape again, so remoulding means giving something a new form.

clue.text: "Leader" is a possible description of Nelson

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the chief person, the number one
second meaning: Admiral Nelson was a man of the main, the old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: Nelson suggests Mandela, a leader; it is really Horatio Nelson, the British naval hero, and 'the main' is poetic for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Main man is informal for the most important person or a boss, and also literally a seafaring man.

clue.text: Drunk liberal punches yours truly in drink

indicators.note: punching into something means going inside it

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, me

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An intoxicated Lib Dem throws a punch at the writer in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirabelle is a small yellow plum and also the clear fruit brandy distilled from it.

clue.text: Ratty men struggling to win one Labour ward?

indicators.note: winning something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside
struggling suggests disorder, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Bad-tempered party workers fighting to take a Labour constituency at an election.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour and ward both read as politics, a party and an electoral district; the question mark marks the pun on childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: A maternity ward is the hospital department where women in labour give birth.

clue.text: Flying saucer?

parts.note: surface reading: an alien spacecraft, a UFO
setter's reading: a plastic disc shaped like a saucer that people throw in the park

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests science fiction, but the object is a toy that is literally a saucer shape sent through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: This toy is a concave plastic disc thrown with a spin so it glides, much like a dish in flight.

clue.text: Somewhat smart Conservative involved in blunder

indicators.note: being involved in something means being inside it

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake
the political right is the conservative side

explanation.surface: A fairly clever Tory has been caught up in a gaffe.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright means intelligent and the -ish suffix softens it to fairly, so it matches a moderate degree of cleverness.

clue.text: Great fried sandwiches at hearty get-together?

indicators.note: to sandwich is to enclose something between two layers
frying changes the form of food, so these letters are cooked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A splendid fry-up of sandwiches served at a cheerful gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearty looks like an adjective for a jolly party, but a hearty is also an old word for a sailor, hence a meeting of boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, an event bringing together seafarers or rowers.

clue.text: Everyone, I must cuddle Republican quickly!

parts.note: everyone is all

indicators.note: a cuddle wraps arms around someone, so one piece holds another

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An urgent appeal: everyone, I need to hug the Republican, and fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark belongs to the definition, which is a musical direction, like an instruction shouted to an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical tempo marking meaning briskly and lively, a fast pace.

clue.text: High-flyer crosses avenue at first green man

indicators.note: something that crosses a thing spans it, so it is placed around it

parts.note: the martin is a swallow-like bird

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of avenue

explanation.surface: An ambitious high-achiever crossing the road when the green walking figure lights up.
explanation.walkthrough: Green man in the surface is the pedestrian crossing signal; as the definition it is a little green man from space.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens from Mars are popularly pictured as little green men, so a green man is a Mars dweller.

clue.text: Portion of cumin or Cajun-style chicken

indicators.note: a portion is a part, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of cumin, all of or and the start of Cajun

explanation.surface: A recipe: some cumin, or chicken done the Louisiana way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minorca is a Mediterranean breed of domestic chicken, named after the Spanish island.

clue.text: Shortly where one'll find old boy in shape

definitions.meaning: first meaning: soon, in a little while

definitions.text: where one'll find old boy in shape
definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: OB, old boy, sits in the shape OBLONG ahead of the rest of that word

explanation.walkthrough: In OBLONG, the letters OB sit in front of LONG, which describes their position as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Before long means soon, a little while from now, which is what shortly means.

clue.text: Lover that has a smoking-hot body?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the burning glowing gas of a fire

explanation.walkthrough: Smoking-hot body suggests an attractive person, keeping the romantic surface, but literally describes fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A flame is slang for a romantic partner, and literally the hot glowing part of a fire.

clue.text: Those starting wars hate all truces, eh?

indicators.note: the starting letters are the opening ones of each word

parts.note: opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: warmongers resent every ceasefire, don't they?
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections asking someone to repeat what they just said.

clue.text: Relationship Congress raised with Germany's No 1

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word turns it to read bottom to top

parts.note: it is slang for sexual intercourse, which congress can also mean
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: Ties between the US Congress and Germany's leader have improved.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the American legislature and No 1 like a leader; they are sex and the German number.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a connection or link between things, a relationship.

clue.text: Sport heading for diving pool

parts.note: sport means fun, as in doing something in sport

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its top, its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of diving

explanation.surface: A sportsperson making for the swimming pool to dive.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool reads as water for swimming, but here it is money pooled together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund is a pooled reserve of money, and a pool is a shared stake or kitty.

clue.text: Principal appealing to Miss Penny

indicators.note: to miss something is to leave it out

parts.note: pleading means appealing or begging
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A head teacher begging a woman called Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Penny reads as a lady's name and title; Miss is really the instruction to drop the penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading means chief or foremost, a synonym for principal as an adjective.

clue.text: Run-of-the-mill performance on Strictly?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dance number, as on the BBC show Strictly Come Dancing

explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a popular BBC ballroom competition, where each couple performs a choreographed number each week.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means ordinary, and as a noun a set sequence of moves in a dance act.

clue.text: Occasionally have on trendy new pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are poor as they stand and need reworking

parts.note: all the letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Sometimes I wear fashionable fresh trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants reads as trousers, the thing being worn, but works as slang for something bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Every now and then means from time to time, an idiom for sometimes.
